<a id="MainBranch"></a>

### How the repository merges into main

`MainBranch` · `src/sdlc.ts:463`

The main branch of the repository receives nothing but pull requests, and is never deleted nor rewritten; a pull request passes the check of each project the repository holds (its job), need not be up to date with main, and merges as a merge commit, which keeps each commit of the branch (a generation is a commit); GitHub may merge it once it holds, when someone asks it to, and deletes its branch then. No approval is required: the workflows keep from merging itself what people decided, which a person merges.

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| branch | main |
| checks | trame, std, ci, data, team, machine, commands, documents, reservations, poselia |
| upToDate | false |
| approvals | 0 |
| method | merge |
| autoMerge | true |
| deletesMerged | true |
| pages | false |

- Decided by: trame
- Rejected: Squashed, a branch would merge as one commit, and the generations it advances are each a commit; An approval required, the person who opens a pull request with their own account cannot approve it; Up to date with main first, each pull request would merge main into itself again, and run its checks again, whenever another one merged; The check of geometry, geometry runs from the registry of a machine, which a runner of GitHub does not have yet; Pages now, the site that gathers Trame's graph and Poselia's preview is still to be decided
- Used by: [Set the repository's settings](#ApplyTheRepositorySettings), [Trame's settings, as std's commands read them](#OurCommandsSettled), [How Trame's pull requests are opened](#OurPullRequests), [Read the repository's settings](#ReadTheRepositorySettings), [The repository is set as the graph decides](#SettingTheRepository)

### How a pull request is checked on GitHub

`PullRequestsOnGitHub` · `src/sdlc.ts:428`

At each pull request into main, on GitHub's Ubuntu 24.04 machine with Node.js 22: its job, named trame, is a check the repository requires; it keeps GitHub from merging a pull request that changes what people decided (a trame.lock of the repository), which a person then merges (D1). It installs Poselia's packages too: the scenarios enter Poselia (ScenarioProjects), whose code uses three.js.

|---|---|
| on | { pullRequests: main } |
| job | trame |
| alsoInstalls | apps/poselia |
| runsOn | ubuntu-24.04 |
| node | 22 |
| artefacts | { days: 30 } |
| pullRequest | { review: false, merge: onceItHoldsUnlessDecided } |

- Decided by: trame
- Rejected: Only when a pull request touches the project, GitHub keeps a pull request waiting for a check it requires and that never ran; Merged by GitHub whatever it changes, what people decided would reach main without a person; The review of the branch, Trame publishes nothing yet: its graph is published once the plan is done

## Message catalog

<a id="SdlcWords"></a>

### What the programs of Trame's SDLC say

`SdlcWords` · `src/sdlc.ts:298`

<details><summary>The messages, in code</summary>

```typescript
() => ({
    advanceUsage: (by: string, accept: string, promote: string) => `Say who advances: trame advance ${by} <name> [${accept}] [${promote} "what changes"]`,
    advanceAssembling: (component: string) => `The generation in place assembles ${component}`,
    advanceStopped: (component: string) => `The advance stopped: ${component} could not be assembled`,
    opens: () => "The graph page opens: its documents, a document shown, its nodes, the figure of the layers drawn, no error",
    noDocuments: () => "The navigation lists no document",
    noDocument: () => "No document is shown",
    noNodes: () => "The picker lists no node",
    noFigureDocument: () => "The navigation has no figure of the layers",
    noFigure: () => "The figure of the layers is not drawn",
    pageError: (error: string) => `The page raised "${error}"`,
    asDecided: (repository: string) => `${repository} holds the settings the graph decides`,
    notAsDecided: (repository: string) => `${repository} does not hold the settings the graph decides:`,
    differs: (part: string, decided: string, found: string) => `  ${part}: decided ${decided}, found ${found}`,
    nothing: () => "nothing",
    set: (repository: string) => `${repository} is set as the graph decides, and read back so`,
    callRefused: (call: string) => `GitHub did not take the call ${call}: only an administrator of the repository may set it`,
    unreadable: (repository: string) => `${repository} cannot be read: GitHub's command line, signed in, reads it`,
  })
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Written in: [Language](messages.md#Language)
- Used by: [Advance](#AdvanceAGeneration), [Set the repository's settings](#ApplyTheRepositorySettings), [The graph page is opened as a person would](#OpeningTheGraphPage), [Open the graph page](#OpenTheGraphPage), [Read the repository's settings](#ReadTheRepositorySettings), [The repository is set as the graph decides](#SettingTheRepository)

Context: The engine's commands reached its modules directly: a project could neither choose them nor specialize them, and a command of its own could not compute what they computed.

### The next generation

`NextGeneration` · `src/sdlc.ts:392` · status: **unknown**

The engine as the graph describes it now, frozen into the next generation and pinned by Trame and the example, the way a generation is made: what it must prove is derived from what the candidate reaches (the laws it plays, the scenarios of its code, the requirements of the goals it serves, the rules, the packages), nothing listed by hand. The advance deploys it, and refuses a candidate the requirement "Accept a candidate" does not accept.

## Policies

<a id="GenerationMode"></a>

### How a generation is made

`GenerationMode` · `src/sdlc.ts:136`

The way Trame advances its engine: the code it reaches verified (a gap is an error), the goals it serves held, the decisions it applies held, the candidate checked by programs, the rules held, the packages safe, its callers identified; and the foundations, as always.

And, as every policy, the foundations: no literal in a body, and a sound graph (nothing undecided, no error of the graph).

- Owner: trame
- Its obligations: [The engine is verified](#EngineVerified), [The language serves what it says](#LanguageServed), [The decisions of the architecture hold](#ArchitectureApplied), [The candidate is checked by programs](#CandidateChecked), [The rules of the architecture hold](#ArchitectureRuled), [The packages are safe](#EnginePackagesSafe), [Its callers identified](#EngineCallersIdentified)
- Followed by: [The next generation](#NextGeneration)

<a id="MergeMode"></a>

### How a change merges

`MergeMode` · `src/sdlc.ts:412`

The way Trame takes a change into its main branch: the code it brings verified (a gap is an error), the rules held; and the foundations, as always. What the candidate of a generation proves besides is the advance's business.

And, as every policy, the foundations: no literal in a body, and a sound graph (nothing undecided, no error of the graph).

- Owner: trame
- Its obligations: [The engine is verified](#EngineVerified), [The rules of the architecture hold](#ArchitectureRuled)
- Followed by: [Into the main branch](#IntoMain)
